newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat futures end higher.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat futures end higher.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed moderately higher, largely following gains in Chicago and Kansas City wheat futures markets, traders said.

Supportive factors included snow early Friday in the Texas panhandle wheat areas and shortcovering amid ideas Thursday's declines were excessive, traders said. Texas wheat sources said the snow may damage wheat weakened by the freeze nearly two weeks ago. However, they said moisture from the snow melt may aid development of tillers not damaged by the freeze.
Gains were limited by talk clear weather next week may allow spring wheat planting in all but the Red River Valley.
Benson Quinn led buying with 800,000 bushels of July and 400,000 of December, they said.
Cargill was featured selling 2.0 million bushels of MGE July wheat and LFG sold 1.0 million September, traders said. Traders said Cargill's selling appeared to be spreading with KCBT July wheat.
MGE spring wheat futures closed up four to 2-1/2 cents with July up four at $4.44-1/2 per bushel.
The MGE reported Friday's estimated volume was 20.149 million bushels of wheat.
